answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-history bond: every agent identity must lock a slashable deposit and build a verifiable record of completed work before it can transact at scale. A flood of fake identities becomes expensive, because each sybil needs its own deposit and slow history - like laying copper wire through basalt, the cost is per meter, not per blueprint. A new identity is like a willow cutting: it may join, but gains real weight only after it has rooted, served others, and survived audits; misbehavior burns its deposit and history, so reputation cannot be cheaply cloned.
